christmas-lights.local_h: Lighting a Nacogdoches house from 70 miles away
local: Nacogdoches sits about 70 miles south of our Longview shop, down past Henderson. That distance is why installs here start at $1,800, where many homes closer in start at $900. The price covers the same full job either way: lights supplied, C9 lines custom-cut to your roofline, takedown in January and storage until next season.

The quote itself does not need a drive. We build a mock-up from a photo of your house and price it from that, so you see where the lights go, in warm white or color, before you book anything. Older streets near downtown and the SFA campus tend to have tall pines and hardwoods close to the house. Send a photo that shows the whole front of the house with the trees in it, and tell us if you want any of them wrapped. You will see the price at the same time as the design, so there are no surprises when we come out to hang it.

Booking opens in early October and installs run through Thanksgiving week, with the calendar filling up fast. For a town this far out we would rather lock your date early than squeeze a trip in late. Patios, retaining walls and drainage are the other jobs we usually make this drive for, so if you have one of those in mind, mention it in the same quote request.
Businesses around downtown and North Street are quoted the same way as homes. Send a photo of the building and tell us how much of it you want lit.

faq.q: Why do Christmas lights cost more in Nacogdoches than in Longview?
faq.a: Installs more than an hour from Longview start at $1,800, and Nacogdoches is about 70 miles out. Most homes closer in start at $900. You get the same job at either price: the lights, custom-cut C9 lines installed to your roofline, takedown in January and storage until next season.

faq.q: Do I need to meet anyone before I get a Nacogdoches quote?
faq.a: No. Send a photo of the front of your house with a quote request. We build a mock-up that shows where the lights go and what color they are, and we quote from that. Once you approve it, we measure each run and custom-cut the lines to fit.

faq.q: Can you light the big pines and hardwoods in my yard?
faq.a: Tree wraps, ground stakes, garland and wreaths are all options. Tell us which trees you want lit and send a photo with them in it. We will tell you from the photo what makes sense for your house and your budget. Bigger trees and more extras raise the price, and the mock-up shows exactly what is included before you book.

faq.q: What happens if a section goes out in December?
faq.a: Service calls during the season are part of the job. Let us know which section is out and we come back to fix it. In January we take everything down and store it, so you never deal with a tangled box in the attic.

faq.q: When should I book Nacogdoches Christmas lights?
faq.a: As early as you can. Booking opens in early October, installs run through Thanksgiving week, and the calendar fills up fast. A town this far out is easier to schedule when we know the date well ahead of time.
